newsitem.title: USA: US Equitable Life Assurance sued over policies.
newsitem.headline: US Equitable Life Assurance sued over policies.

text.p: Equitable Life Assurance Society of the United States is being sued over its practices in selling variable life insurance policies, a law firm said Friday.

The law firm of Berman, DeValerio & Pease LLP said in a statement that it filed a class-action lawsuit against the company on behalf of Massachusetts residents who purchased the policies between January 9, 1993, and the present.
Equitable Life Assurance is an operating unit of Equitable Cos Inc.
A company spokesman did not immediately have a comment, saying he had not yet seen the lawsuit.

The complaint alleges that Equitable Life Assurance marketed its variable life insurance policies as a means of savings, "while misrepresenting or failing to properly disclose the substantial fees, charges and life insurance costs," the law firm said in a statement.
The complaint contends the company's sales practices for those policies violated the Massachusetts consumer protection act and state securities laws, and amounted to a breach of contract.
"We have reviewed the allegations contained in the complaint and have determined that they are without merit," company spokesman Jim Lacey said later Friday.

"The named policyholder purchased a variable life insurance policy which is sold with a prospectus. At minimum, the plain language of the policy and the prospectus state that the policyholder was purchasing life insurance and described fees, charges and cost of insurance," Lacey said.
"We intend to vigorously defend the lawsuit," he added. Friday, 25 April 1997 17:02:40 ENDS nN25281386
